item.text: {"text":"BERT4Rec explicitly specifies terminal-mask training, separately from appended-mask inference. Section 3.6 describes random masking of a proportion of sequence items, predicting them using available left and right context. It additionally produces training examples that mask only the input sequence’s final item, describing this as analogous to fine-tuning for sequential recommendation. At inference, it appends a new [mask] token and scores the next item from that token’s representation. Thus, terminal-mask supervision is explicitly part of training; it is not merely inferred from the inference procedure. [Original paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690#S3.SS6)\n\nThe paper does not specify randomly sampling arbitrary prefix endpoints and removing all subsequent context as its training augmentation. Indeed, §3.6 discusses constructing a separate prefix–next-item example for every position, but calls that approach computationally expensive and introduces Cloze training instead. Its stated combinatorial sample expansion comes from different masking patterns over a sequence, not arbitrary prefix truncation. Masking the last item of a supplied sequence and choosing an arbitrary historical item to become a truncated sequence’s endpoint are distinct sampling policies. Consequently, attributing arbitrary-prefix terminal-mask sampling to the original paper requires additional evidence; appended-mask inference and final-item training alone do not establish that policy. [Original paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690#S3.SS6)"}
